learn.hook: You run a full lap of the school ground and end up exactly where you started. You are tired, but how far have you really moved from the start? Physics gives two answers!
points: Motion is always described relative to a reference point. A passenger sitting in a moving train is at rest relative to the train but in motion relative to the platform.
Distance is the total length of the path travelled. It has only magnitude, so it is a scalar quantity.
Displacement is the shortest straight-line distance from the starting point to the final point, in a stated direction. It has magnitude and direction, so it is a vector quantity.
Displacement can be zero even when distance is not, for example after one full round of a track.
The magnitude of displacement can never be greater than the distance travelled. The SI unit of both is the metre (m).

example.q: Think it through: Kiran walks 6 km east from her house to a market and then 2 km west to a temple. Find the distance and the displacement.
steps: Distance = total path = 6 km + 2 km = 8 km.
Displacement looks only at start and end points.
She ends 6 − 2 = 4 km east of her house.
So displacement = 4 km towards the east.

learn.reallife: An auto-rickshaw meter charges for distance travelled along the roads, while a map's straight 'as the crow flies' line shows displacement.

games.title: Distance or displacement?
items: Displacement can be zero even if an object has moved
If the object comes back to its starting point, its displacement is zero.
Distance is a vector quantity
Distance has only magnitude, so it is a scalar. Displacement is the vector.
The magnitude of displacement can never be more than the distance travelled
The straight line between two points is the shortest path, so it can never be longer than the actual path.
A passenger sitting in a moving bus is at rest relative to the bus
The passenger's position does not change compared with the bus seats.
Displacement is measured along the actual path taken
Displacement is measured along the straight line from start to finish, not along the path.

items.q: 3 m east, then 4 m north: displacement?
3 m east, then 4 m north: distance?
10 m north, then 4 m south: displacement?
10 m north, then 4 m south: distance?
Half a lap of a 400 m track: distance?
5 m forward, then 5 m back: displacement?

quiz.q: Neha runs exactly one round of a 400 m circular track and stops at the start line. What are her distance and displacement?
quiz.explain: She covered a path of 400 m, but she ended where she began, so her displacement is zero.
quiz.mistake: Treats distance and displacement as the same quantity

quiz.q: Aman walks 3 m east and then 4 m north. What is the magnitude of his displacement?
quiz.explain: The two walks are at right angles, so the straight line from start to end is the hypotenuse: √(3² + 4²) = 5 m.
quiz.mistake: Adds the two walks, which gives distance, not displacement

quiz.q: Kiran walks 6 km east and then 2 km west. What is the magnitude of her displacement?
quiz.explain: The walks are in opposite directions, so she ends 6 − 2 = 4 km east of her start.
quiz.mistake: Adds the two parts, which gives the distance of 8 km

quiz.q: Which of these is a vector quantity?
quiz.explain: Displacement has both magnitude and direction. Distance, time and mass have only magnitude.
quiz.mistake: Thinks any measured length is a vector

quiz.q: A boy walks along a curved road from his house to school. Compared with the distance, the magnitude of his displacement is
quiz.explain: A curved path is longer than the straight line joining its ends, so displacement is less than distance.
quiz.mistake: Thinks displacement can be longer than the path walked

quiz.q: Riya is sitting in a moving train. Relative to which of these is she at rest?
options: The seat she is sitting on
quiz.explain: Her position does not change relative to the seat, which moves with her. Relative to the ground, she is moving.
quiz.mistake: Thinks rest and motion are absolute, not relative to a reference point

quiz.q: What is the SI unit of displacement?
quiz.explain: Displacement is a length, so its SI unit is the metre.
quiz.mistake: Confuses the unit of length with units of speed or force

quiz.q: Sameer climbs 3 floors up and then comes back down to the ground floor. Which statement is correct?
options: His displacement equals the distance he travelled
His displacement is zero but the distance is not
Both distance and displacement are zero
quiz.explain: He ended at his starting point, so displacement is zero, but he did travel along the stairs, so distance is not zero.
quiz.mistake: Thinks returning to the start cancels the distance too

teach.ask: Gappu flew from his nest to a pond and back home: "My wings are tired, but my teacher says I moved ZERO. How can that be?"
teach.praise: Chirp! Distance counts my whole flight, but displacement is only the straight line from start to finish with a direction. I came back home, so it is zero!
teach.nudge: So which one counts my whole flight path, and which one only looks at where I started and ended?

learn.hook: The Vande Bharat express speeds up smoothly out of a station and slows down before the next one. How do we describe how fast it goes and how fast its speed changes?
points: Speed = distance ÷ time. Its SI unit is m/s. Average speed = total distance ÷ total time taken.
Velocity is speed in a stated direction: velocity = displacement ÷ time. It is a vector.
Acceleration is the rate of change of velocity: a = (v − u) ÷ t, where u is the initial velocity and v is the final velocity. Its SI unit is m/s².
If velocity decreases, acceleration is negative (called deceleration or retardation). Uniform motion means equal distances in equal intervals of time.
In uniform circular motion the speed stays the same but the direction keeps changing, so the velocity changes and the motion is accelerated. To change km/h to m/s, multiply by 5/18.

example.q: Think it through: A car starts from rest and reaches 72 km/h in 10 s. What is its acceleration?
steps: u = 0 (starts from rest), v = 20 m/s, t = 10 s.

learn.reallife: Speed limit boards on Indian highways, speedometers in buses and the cricket radar that shows how fast a fast bowler delivers the ball all measure speed.

items.text: Velocity is speed in a given ___.
If a scooter slows down, its acceleration is ___.
An object moving with constant velocity has ___ acceleration.
In uniform circular motion the ___ keeps changing.

quiz.q: A bus covers 120 km in 3 hours. What is its average speed in km/h?
quiz.explain: Average speed = total distance ÷ total time = 120 ÷ 3 = 40 km/h.
quiz.mistake: Multiplies distance by time instead of dividing

quiz.q: A train runs at 72 km/h. What is its speed in m/s?
quiz.mistake: Multiplies by 18/5 instead of 5/18

quiz.q: A car starts from rest and reaches 20 m/s in 5 s. What is its acceleration in m/s²?
quiz.mistake: Divides time by velocity or multiplies them

quiz.q: A motorbike slows from 15 m/s to 5 m/s in 5 s. What is its acceleration in m/s²?
quiz.explain: a = (v − u) ÷ t = (5 − 15) ÷ 5 = −2 m/s². The minus sign shows it is slowing down.
steps: u = 15 m/s, v = 5 m/s, t = 5 s
quiz.mistake: Drops the negative sign for slowing down

quiz.q: Why is a child on a merry-go-round turning at a steady speed said to be accelerating?
options: Because the direction of motion keeps changing
Because the child is at rest
quiz.explain: Velocity includes direction. In circular motion the direction changes every moment, so the velocity changes and there is acceleration.
quiz.mistake: Thinks acceleration means only speeding up

quiz.q: What is the main difference between speed and velocity?
options: Velocity has a direction, speed does not
Speed has a direction, velocity does not
Velocity is measured only in km/h
quiz.explain: Both are measured in m/s, but velocity is a vector with a direction, while speed is a scalar.
quiz.mistake: Uses the words speed and velocity as if they mean the same

quiz.q: Rohan cycles 10 km to his tuition centre and comes back home by the same road. What is his average velocity for the whole trip, in km/h?
quiz.explain: He ends where he started, so his total displacement is zero, and average velocity = displacement ÷ time = 0.
quiz.mistake: Uses total distance instead of displacement for velocity

quiz.q: A car moves on a straight road with a constant velocity of 15 m/s. What is its acceleration in m/s²?
quiz.explain: Acceleration is the change in velocity per second. If velocity does not change, acceleration is zero.
quiz.mistake: Thinks a moving object must have acceleration

teach.ask: Gappu zooms around in circles at the same speed: "My friend says I am accelerating. But I am not going any faster! Who is right?"
teach.praise: Tweet! Velocity includes direction, and acceleration is any change in velocity. Turning in a circle changes my direction, so I really am accelerating!
teach.nudge: Is velocity just about how fast I go, or does it also care about which way I go?

learn.hook: Before a cricket ball even lands, physics can tell you where it will land. For motion with uniform acceleration, three short equations do the job!
points: For uniform acceleration along a straight line: v = u + at, s = ut + ½at², and v² = u² + 2as, where s is the displacement.
On a distance–time graph, a horizontal line means the object is at rest; a straight sloping line means uniform speed; the slope gives the speed.
On a velocity–time graph, a horizontal line means uniform velocity; a straight sloping line means uniform acceleration; the slope gives the acceleration.
The area under a velocity–time graph gives the displacement.
Always change units to m and s before using the equations.

example.q: Think it through: A car moving at 20 m/s brakes with a uniform acceleration of −4 m/s². How far does it travel before stopping?
steps: u = 20 m/s, v = 0 (it stops), a = −4 m/s².
We do not know t, so use v² = u² + 2as.

learn.reallife: Road safety engineers use these equations to work out braking distances and decide speed limits near schools.

games.title: Solving a motion problem
games.prompt: Arrange the steps for solving a motion problem
items: List the known quantities with units
Write down the quantity you need to find
Choose the equation that links them
Substitute the values
Calculate and write the answer with its unit

quiz.q: A train starts from rest with an acceleration of 2 m/s². What is its velocity after 10 s, in m/s?
quiz.mistake: Adds a and t instead of multiplying

quiz.q: The same train (starting from rest, a = 2 m/s²) travels how far in those 10 s?
quiz.explain: s = ut + ½at² = 0 + ½ × 2 × 10² = 100 m.
quiz.mistake: Forgets the ½ or forgets to square the time

quiz.q: A car at 20 m/s brakes with an acceleration of −4 m/s². What distance does it cover before it stops?
quiz.mistake: Forgets the factor 2 in 2as, getting 100 m

quiz.q: On a distance–time graph, a horizontal straight line shows that the object is
quiz.explain: A horizontal line means the distance is not changing as time passes, so the object is not moving.
quiz.mistake: Confuses a distance–time graph with a velocity–time graph

quiz.q: The slope of a velocity–time graph gives the
quiz.explain: Slope = change in velocity ÷ time, which is the definition of acceleration.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the slope with the area under the graph

quiz.q: What does the area under a velocity–time graph give?
quiz.explain: Velocity × time = displacement, so the area between the graph and the time axis gives the displacement.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the area gives acceleration, which is the slope

quiz.q: A velocity–time graph is a straight line from 0 m/s at t = 0 to 10 m/s at t = 5 s. What is the displacement in these 5 s?
quiz.explain: The area under the line is a triangle: ½ × base × height = ½ × 5 × 10 = 25 m.
steps: Area of triangle = ½ × base × height
quiz.mistake: Uses base × height and forgets the ½ for a triangle

quiz.q: Which equation would you use to find the final velocity when you know u, a and s, but not t?
quiz.explain: v² = u² + 2as links v, u, a and s without needing the time.
quiz.mistake: Picks an equation that needs the unknown time

teach.ask: Gappu stares at a graph: "My teacher drew a sloping line on a velocity–time graph. What can I learn from a graph like this?"
teach.praise: Chirp chirp! The slope of a velocity–time graph tells me the acceleration, and the area under it tells me the displacement. Graphs talk!
teach.nudge: The slope tells me one thing, but what does the area under the line tell me?
